title: Nicole Castillo
content:
Nicole Castillo

Available Virtually + Seattle-Area In Person

Biography

Hi! My name is Nicole, I love my cat, my partner, and learning about mental health and neurodiversity. I have allowed it to seep into every aspect of my life. Problem? Not really! Over the years my passion for these things has helped me to connect deeper with those I care for and has allowed me to reach this space where I can care for more than just my circle of people. Being a part of the LSA team is a dream, I can flex my personality and the skills I’ve been using for years in a functional format to educate and support others. My clients are my top priority, I work with their support systems to create a healing environment for them. I truly take the time to get to know them as well as how they operate. My experience is mainly in ADHD, Depression, and Anxiety, but I am constantly broadening my understanding of different diagnoses like ASD, OCD, and possibly whatever you are seeking help for. My determination to stay educated has pushed me to do better for myself, my circle, and my clients.

What Does Executive Functioning Mean to You?

EF is a skill set that everyone has but is more difficult to use when you are neurodiverse. EF looks like getting a glass of water for yourself, going to the store, and quickly grabbing what you need. Executive DYSfunction is when those “simple” tasks get too overwhelming and add to the difficulties of daily life. That’s where I come in and show you how to hone your EF skills in a way that works for you and I will support you in meeting those goals. 

What Is a Strategy You Use With Clients and Use Personally?

You’ll hear me use “Thought/Feeling Notation” a ton and the mantra "Progress not Perfection". I’ll explain more in session! 

How Has Your Personal Experience and Professional Development Impacted Your Coaching?

Mental health and neurodiversity have been the fully long-term passions that have motivated me to better myself. Personally, I’ve helped people around me function within their diagnoses and find ways to help them communicate their needs and how to meet them themselves. Professionally, I tend to take lead a lot, which helps me naturally guide sessions.

I apply my real-world experience in many different ways and can showcase how a tool for one problem, can be used in several different areas.

How Would You Describe Your Personal Approach to Coaching?

I like to spend the first sessions getting to know my clients and providing a safe space for them to explain what needs aren’t being met and allow them to have frustrations about the things that are difficult. In this stage you’ll hear me use a ton of active listening, hold compassion for you and extend empathy and understanding for your experience. Past that we create a game plan and start working on the issues that have been spoken about previously. I will work with my client to build tools and regimens that are interesting and unique to them that help keeps them motivated toward making progress. I advocate for my younger clients and help bridge the gap for parents to help them understand their child/teenagers' needs. Overall my clients and their support system will receive a ton of compassion, understanding, and someone who will motivate and support them. 

Which of LSA's Core Values Resonates the Most With You, and How Do You Incorporate It With Your Clients?

Personally, the holistic value resonates with me deeply. I can’t help anyone unless I know why they need my help, how they need it, and when and where it needs to be directed. Having a deeper understanding helps me to conceptualize in my space what can and needs to be done to help you reach your goals. 

Do You Have an Area of Coaching You Specialize In?

Time management, mindfulness, shifting mindset, everyday EF, vocational skills, general support, motivation, and accountability. Anything I’m not specialized in I research to better educate myself, my specializations shift constantly.
